file.content:
# Improving the Ingredient Parser

Mealie uses Conditional Random Fields (CRFs) for parsing and processing ingredients. The model used for ingredients is based off a data set of over 100,000 ingredients from a dataset compiled by the New York Times. I believe that the model used is sufficient enough to handle most of the ingredients, therefore, more data to train the model won't necessarily help improve the model.

## Improving The CRF Parser

To improve results with the model, you'll likely need to focus on improving the tokenization and parsing of the original string to aid the model in determine what the ingredient is. Data science is not my forte, but I have done some tokenization to improve the model. You can find that code under `/mealie/services/parser_services/crfpp` along with some other utility functions to aid in the tokenization and processing of ingredient strings.

The best way to test on improving the parser is to register additional test cases in  `/mealie/tests/unit_tests/test_crfpp_parser.py` and run the test after making changes to the tokenizer. Note that the test cases DO NOT run in the CI environment, therefore you will need to have CRF++ installed on your machine. If you're using a Mac the easiest way to do this is through brew.

When submitting a PR to improve the parser it is important to provide your test cases, the problem you were trying to solve, and the results of the changes you made. As the tests don't run in CI, not providing these details may delay your PR from being merged.

## Alternative Parsers
Alternatively, you can register a new parser by fulfilling the `ABCIngredientParser` interface. Satisfying this single method interface allows us to register additional parsing strategies at runtime and gives the user several options when trying to parse a recipe.


## Links
- [Pretrained Model](https://github.com/mealie-recipes/mealie-nlp-model)
- [CRF++ (Forked)](https://github.com/hay-kot/crfpp)

content.text:
To add a strategy, you add a parser class, extend the `RegisteredParser` enum, and wire it into the factory. The API routes themselves need no change.

**What the docs say.** The contributor guide's "Alternative Parsers" section says to register a new parser by fulfilling the `ABCIngredientParser` interface. That interface is a single-method contract, and it is what lets additional strategies be registered at runtime and offered to users. The same guide's "Improving The CRF Parser" section applies only if you want to improve the existing CRF/NLP tokenizer. It points to `mealie/services/parser_services/crfpp` and to the tests in `test_crfpp_parser.py`. Those tests don't run in CI, so a PR needs your own test cases and results. The AI providers page mentions that users pick the parser (NLP, brute force or AI) when parsing ingredients. That tells you the selection is user-facing.

**What must change**
1. **Parser class.** Write a subclass of `ABCIngredientParser` (`mealie/services/parser_services/_base.py:130`). The existing subclasses are `BruteForceParser`, `NLPParser` (both in `ingredient_parser.py`) and `OpenAIParser` (`openai/parser.py`), and they are the templates. They implement `parse_one` and `parse`, and they reuse the base class's `find_ingredient_match`.
2. **Enum.** Add a member to `RegisteredParser` (`mealie/schema/recipe/recipe_ingredient.py:519`). This is the value API clients send.
3. **Factory.** In `mealie/services/parser_services/ingredient_parser.py`, add your class to the private `__registrar` dict (around line 312). `get_parser` (line 318) looks the enum up there. Two behaviours to know:
   - `get_parser` special-cases `openai` with a lazy import. A heavy or optional dependency would need the same treatment.
   - Any enum value missing from the registrar silently falls back to `NLPParser`. If you add the enum member but forget the registrar entry, requests will quietly use NLP.

**What is affected**
- `IngredientRequest` and `IngredientsRequest` (`recipe_ingredient.py:530` and `:525`) use `RegisteredParser`. The new enum value flows into the request schemas and the generated OpenAPI schema automatically.
- `IngredientParserController.parse_ingredient` and `parse_ingredients` (`mealie/routes/parser/ingredient_parser.py`) are the only callers of `get_parser`. They need no change.
- The `mealie.schema.recipe` package re-exports `RegisteredParser`.
- If the frontend has a parser dropdown or TypeScript types for this enum, they would need updating too. I didn't check that.
